fhb-low-deposit.html: In September 2026, 50.3% of first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) were written with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR), up from 46.0% a year earlier.
fhb-low-deposit.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 1,342 high-LVR (>80% LVR) FHB borrowers ($850m) out of 2,667 total FHB borrowers ($1,530m).
fhb-low-deposit.source_html:
HLF calculation: 1,342 ÷ 2,667 = 50.3% (Lending: $850m ÷ $1,530m = 55.6%)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
fhb-low-deposit.name: First-home buyers using under 20% deposit (>80% LVR)
fhb-low-deposit.also_known_as: Low-deposit first-home buyer mortgage share / High-LVR (>80%) FHB share
fhb-low-deposit.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31)
fhb-low-deposit.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived percentage share
fhb-low-deposit.definition: The percentage of new first-home buyer residential mortgage commitments approved by New Zealand registered banks with a loan-to-value ratio (LVR) above 80% (meaning a deposit of less than 20%).
fhb-low-deposit.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: First-home buyers are the primary recipients of bank low-deposit (>80% LVR) lending allowances, supplemented by LVR-exempt Kāinga Ora First Home Loans and new-build lending.
fhb-low-deposit.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 by dividing the monthly number of new first-home buyer mortgage commitments with LVR > 80% (LVRN.MMB2.BC1) by total monthly first-home buyer mortgage commitments (LVRN.MMB2.AC1), multiplied by 100.
fhb-low-deposit.summary_text: In September 2026, 50.3% of first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) were written with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR), up from 46.0% a year earlier.
fhb-low-deposit.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "First-home buyers using under 20% deposit (>80% LVR)," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-low-deposit/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.

fhb-share.html: In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 2,667 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $1.53B—accounting for 20.3% of all new residential mortgage lending (up from 19.2% a year earlier), with an average loan size of $573,678.
fhb-share.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 2,667 FHB borrowers and $1,530m FHB lending out of $7,533m total new residential lending (LVRN.MMB1.AA).
fhb-share.source_html:
HLF calculation: $1,530m ÷ $7,533m = 20.3% (Mean loan: $1,530m × $1m ÷ 2,667 = $573,678; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
fhb-share.calculation_live: $1,530m ÷ $7,533m = 20.3% (Mean loan: $1,530m × $1m ÷ 2,667 = $573,678; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
fhb-share.name: First-home buyer share of new mortgage lending & average loan size
fhb-share.also_known_as: FHB share of total residential mortgage commitments & mean FHB loan value
fhb-share.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31)
fhb-share.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived share/mean
fhb-share.definition: The share of total new residential mortgage lending value committed to first-home buyers across New Zealand, alongside the monthly number of first-home buyer loans and mean loan size.
fhb-share.calculation: $1,530m ÷ $7,533m = 20.3% (Mean loan: $1,530m × $1m ÷ 2,667 = $573,678; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
fhb-share.formula: (FHB Lending Value [LVRN.MMB1.AC1] ÷ All-Borrower Total Lending [LVRN.MMB1.AA]) × 100; Mean Loan = LVRN.MMB1.AC1 ÷ LVRN.MMB2.AC1
fhb-share.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Tracks first-home buyer market participation relative to existing owner-occupiers and residential property investors.
fhb-share.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 by dividing first-home buyer new lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AC1) by total new lending across all borrower types (LVRN.MMB1.AA). Mean loan size is LVRN.MMB1.AC1 (published by RBNZ rounded to $1m) divided by LVRN.MMB2.AC1.
fhb-share.summary_text: In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 2,667 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $1.53B—accounting for 20.3% of all new residential mortgage lending (up from 19.2% a year earlier), with an average loan size of $573,678.
fhb-share.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "First-home buyer share of new mortgage lending & average loan size," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fhb-share/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.

refinance.html: In September 2026, 2,772 New Zealand mortgage holders switched lenders, refinancing $1.73B ($1,729m) in home loans—representing 23.0% of all new residential mortgage lending, at an average loan size of $623,737.
refinance.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Change in loan provider = 2,772 borrowers and $1,729m out of $7,533m total purpose lending (dollar series rounded to $1m).
refinance.source_html:
HLF calculation: $1,729m ÷ $7,533m = 23.0% (Mean loan: $1,729m × $1m ÷ 2,772 = $623,737; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33) • Direct RBNZ C33 .xlsx • Glossary: Refinancing · Usable Equity • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
refinance.calculation_live: $1,729m ÷ $7,533m = 23.0% (Mean loan: $1,729m × $1m ÷ 2,772 = $623,737; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
refinance.name: Mortgage refinancing (switching loan provider) share & volume
refinance.also_known_as: Bank-to-bank mortgage switching share, loan count & average refinance size
refinance.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33)
refinance.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived share/mean
refinance.definition: The share of new residential mortgage lending value and number of borrowers switching from one mortgage lender to another ('change in loan provider'), alongside the mean refinanced loan size.
refinance.calculation: $1,729m ÷ $7,533m = 23.0% (Mean loan: $1,729m × $1m ÷ 2,772 = $623,737; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
refinance.formula: (Change in Loan Provider Value [LVRN.MMB1.AZD] ÷ Total Lending by Purpose) × 100; Mean Loan = LVRN.MMB1.AZD ÷ LVRN.MMB2.AZD
refinance.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Refinancing volume measures how actively existing mortgage holders are comparing fixed rates and cashback offers across competing banks once their fixed terms expire.
refinance.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C33 by dividing 'change in loan provider' lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AZD) by the sum of all purpose categories (property purchase AZC, top-up AZB, change in provider AZD, and other AZE).
refinance.summary_text: In September 2026, 2,772 New Zealand mortgage holders switched lenders, refinancing $1.73B ($1,729m) in home loans—representing 23.0% of all new residential mortgage lending, at an average loan size of $623,737.
refinance.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Mortgage refinancing (switching loan provider) share & volume," September 2026. top-ups.html: In September 2026, 9,639 homeowners were approved for a mortgage top-up on their existing property—accounting for 46.4% of all mortgage approvals across New Zealand, with an average top-up of $99,803.
top-ups.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Top-up approvals = 9,639 borrowers ($962m) out of 20,763 total approvals.
top-ups.source_html:
HLF calculation: 9,639 ÷ 20,763 = 46.4% (Mean top-up: $962m × $1m ÷ 9,639 = $99,803)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33) • Direct RBNZ C33 .xlsx • Glossary: Refinancing · Usable Equity • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
top-ups.name: Mortgage top-up share of approvals & average top-up amount
top-ups.also_known_as: Existing homeowner equity top-up approval share & mean top-up value
top-ups.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33)
top-ups.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived share/mean
top-ups.definition: The percentage of all monthly residential mortgage approvals that are top-ups on an existing mortgage with the same lender, alongside the mean dollar top-up size.
top-ups.formula: (Top-up Count [LVRN.MMB2.AZB] ÷ Total Approvals by Purpose) × 100; Mean Top-Up = LVRN.MMB1.AZB ÷ LVRN.MMB2.AZB
top-ups.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Top-ups are one of the most common transactions in New Zealand banking—used by homeowners to fund renovations, deposits on investment properties, or major capital purchases.
top-ups.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C33 by dividing top-up borrower count (LVRN.MMB2.AZB) by total mortgage approvals across all purposes, and dividing top-up lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AZB, rounded to $1m) by top-up borrower count.
top-ups.summary_text: In September 2026, 9,639 homeowners were approved for a mortgage top-up on their existing property—accounting for 46.4% of all mortgage approvals across New Zealand, with an average top-up of $99,803.
top-ups.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Mortgage top-up share of approvals & average top-up amount," September 2026. rent-yield-pulse.html: In September 2026, New Zealand's national median weekly private rent was $599/wk (up 1.5% year-on-year), with regional medians of $640/wk in Auckland, $580/wk in Wellington, and $560/wk in Canterbury.
rent-yield-pulse.official_data_summary: MBIE Tenancy Services (September 2026): National ('ALL') median weekly rent = $599/wk; Auckland = $640/wk; Wellington = $580/wk; Canterbury = $560/wk.
rent-yield-pulse.source_html:
HLF calculation: Reported national median = $599/wk; YoY = ($599 - $590) ÷ $590 = +1.5%
Source: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — Tenancy Services Rental Bond Data • Glossary: Gross Rental Yield • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
rent-yield-pulse.source_published: Monthly MBIE Tenancy Services rental bond release (~6–8 weeks after reference month-end)
rent-yield-pulse.name: National & regional median weekly private rent (Auckland, Wellington, Canterbury)
rent-yield-pulse.also_known_as: MBIE Tenancy Services median weekly rent across New Zealand
rent-yield-pulse.source_full: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — Tenancy Services Rental Bond Data
rent-yield-pulse.source_series_ids: MBIE By-Region Rental Bond CSV — Location 'ALL', 'Auckland', 'Wellington', 'Canterbury' Median Rent
rent-yield-pulse.data_type: Officially reported MBIE medians & HLF-derived YoY change
rent-yield-pulse.definition: The national median weekly rent across newly lodged private residential tenancy bonds in New Zealand, alongside regional medians for Auckland, Wellington, and Canterbury.
rent-yield-pulse.formula: YoY Rent Change (%) = ((Current National Median Rent - Prior Year Median Rent) ÷ Prior Year Median Rent) × 100
rent-yield-pulse.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Rental bond medians reflect the actual rents agreed on newly signed tenancies each month, which banks use alongside council rates and insurance when assessing rental yield and investor servicing.
rent-yield-pulse.methodology: Extracted from MBIE Tenancy Services' monthly regional rental bond dataset (Location = 'ALL' for national median), with year-on-year dollar and percentage changes calculated against the same month a year earlier.
rent-yield-pulse.summary_text: In September 2026, New Zealand's national median weekly private rent was $599/wk (up 1.5% year-on-year), with regional medians of $640/wk in Auckland, $580/wk in Wellington, and $560/wk in Canterbury.

kiwisaver-first-home.source_html:
HLF calculation: Monthly mean: $195.7m × $1m ÷ 4,250 = $46,047/member | 10Y annual: $2,270m ÷ $495m = +358.6% nominal (+243.0% real ÷ 1.337 CPI)

interest-only.source_html:

Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New and existing residential mortgage lending by payment type (Table C32) • Direct RBNZ C32 .xlsx • Glossary: Interest-Only Mortgage · KiwiSaver First-Home Withdrawal • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

interest-only.definition: The percentage of new residential mortgage lending written on interest-only terms (including revolving credit facilities) for property investors compared with owner-occupiers.

dti-headroom.html: In September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($139.0m of $1,527.0m)—sitting 10.9 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.
dti-headroom.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C40 (September 2026): FHB lending with TDTI > 6 = $139.0m out of $1,527.0m total FHB commitments.
dti-headroom.source_html:
HLF calculation: $139.0m ÷ $1,527.0m = 9.1% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.1% = 10.9 pts)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income (DTI) purpose use (Table C40) • Direct RBNZ C40 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
dti-headroom.name: First-home buyer high Debt-to-Income (>6x DTI) share vs 20% RBNZ speed limit
dti-headroom.also_known_as: FHB TDTI > 6 share of commitments & buffer below RBNZ DTI speed limit
dti-headroom.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income (DTI) purpose use (Table C40)
dti-headroom.source_series_ids: FHB New Commitments with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB New Commitments
dti-headroom.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived >6x DTI share
dti-headroom.definition: The percentage of total monthly first-home buyer mortgage lending value committed at a Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) ratio above 6x gross income, compared against the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap on non-exempt owner-occupier lending.
dti-headroom.formula: (FHB Lending with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB Commitments across all TDTI bands) × 100; Headroom = 20.0% minus (>6x Share)
dti-headroom.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because bank test servicing rates already constrain borrowing capacity, total FHB lending above 6x DTI sits well inside the 20% RBNZ speed-limit allowance.
dti-headroom.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C40 by summing first-home buyer lending commitments in bands above 6x TDTI (including unknown TDTI) and dividing by total first-home buyer commitments across all TDTI bands.
dti-headroom.summary_text: In September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($139.0m of $1,527.0m)—sitting 10.9 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.

fhb-loan-size-gap.source_html:
HLF calculation: ($850m × $1m ÷ 1,342 = $633,383) minus ($680m × $1m ÷ 1,325 = $513,208) = $120,175 (subject to RBNZ $1m rounding)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

fhb-loan-size-gap.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 by dividing >80% LVR FHB lending value (LVRN.MMB1.BC1) by >80% LVR FHB loan count (LVRN.MMB2.BC1), and comparing against <=80% LVR FHB lending value divided by <=80% LVR FHB loan count.

borrower-income.html: In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands).
borrower-income.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Figures (pools rounded to $0.1m, averages to $1,000): TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 avg ($59.0m pool / 299.5 implied apps) | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 avg ($101.0m pool / 668.9 implied apps) | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 avg ($124.0m pool / 892.1 implied apps) | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 avg ($76.0m pool / 608.0 implied apps) | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000 avg ($23.0m pool / 187.0 implied apps).
borrower-income.source_html:
HLF calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41) • Direct RBNZ C41 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
borrower-income.calculation_live: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding)
borrower-income.name: Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs property investors
borrower-income.also_known_as: Borrower Gross Income (BGI) mean across approved FHB & investor applications (RBNZ C41)
borrower-income.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41)
borrower-income.source_series_ids: Sum(Band Total Gross Income) ÷ Sum(Band Implied Borrowers) across TDTI bands
borrower-income.data_type: HLF-derived band-weighted mean from official RBNZ Table C41 bands
borrower-income.definition: The band-weighted mean annual gross borrower income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications and property investor applications, derived by HLF from RBNZ Table C41's Debt-to-Income bands.
borrower-income.calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding)
borrower-income.formula: Sum(Band Total Gross Income [$m]) ÷ Sum(Band Total Gross Income [$m] ÷ Band Average Gross Income [$k]) × 1,000
borrower-income.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: RBNZ's Borrower Gross Income (BGI) measures total application income (which for couples combines two salaries, and for investors includes existing salaries plus gross rental and other qualifying income).
borrower-income.methodology: RBNZ Table C41 publishes official total gross income ($m, rounded to $0.1m) and average gross income ($000, rounded to $1,000) within each TDTI band rather than a single all-bands average. HLF derives the overall mean by dividing total gross income summed across all reported TDTI bands by the implied number of applications (Band Total Income ÷ Band Average Income) summed across those bands.
borrower-income.summary_text: In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands).
borrower-income.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs property investors," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.

fhb-regional-kiwisaver.source_html:

Source: Inland Revenue — KiwiSaver Fund Withdrawals by Region (Annual June Financial Year) • Glossary: KiwiSaver First-Home Withdrawal • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

fhb-regional-kiwisaver.formula: Regional Average Withdrawal ($) = Regional First-Home Withdrawal Dollars ÷ Regional First-Home Withdrawing Members
fhb-regional-kiwisaver.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Higher-priced regions such as Auckland, Tasman, Wellington, and Bay of Plenty record larger average KiwiSaver first-home withdrawals per member than lower-priced regions.
fhb-regional-kiwisaver.methodology: Derived from Inland Revenue's annual regional KiwiSaver withdrawal tables by dividing each region's first-home withdrawal dollar total by the number of withdrawing members in that region.

investor-low-deposit.html: In September 2026, 52 property investor mortgages ($36m) were approved with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR, or 1.9% of investors, up from 34 loans a year earlier) (508 loans / $328m over the past 12 months), alongside 475 investor loans ($301m, or 17.8%) in the 70%–80% LVR band.
investor-low-deposit.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): >80% LVR investors = 52 loans ($36m); >70% LVR investors = 527 loans ($337m).
investor-low-deposit.source_html:
HLF calculation: >80% LVR: 52 ÷ 2,668 = 1.9% ($36m) | 70–80% LVR: 527 - 52 = 475 loans ($301m)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

investor-low-deposit.definition: Monthly count and dollar value of residential property investor mortgage commitments approved at >80% LVR (under 20% deposit) and in the 70%–80% LVR band (20%–30% deposit).
investor-low-deposit.formula: >80% LVR = LVRN.MMB2.BN; 70%–80% LVR = LVRN.MMB2.DN minus LVRN.MMB2.BN
investor-low-deposit.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Under RBNZ LVR rules, new builds are exempt from LVR speed limits, allowing eligible new-build investors to borrow at 80% LVR (a 20% deposit) alongside discretionary bank speed-limit allowances.
investor-low-deposit.methodology: Extracted from RBNZ Table C31 series LVRN.MMB2.BN / LVRN.MMB1.BN (>80% LVR investors), with the 70%–80% LVR band derived by subtracting >80% LVR investor commitments from >70% LVR investor commitments (LVRN.MMB2.DN / LVRN.MMB1.DN).
investor-low-deposit.summary_text: In September 2026, 52 property investor mortgages ($36m) were approved with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR, or 1.9% of investors, up from 34 loans a year earlier) (508 loans / $328m over the past 12 months), alongside 475 investor loans ($301m, or 17.8%) in the 70%–80% LVR band.

natural-hazard-claims.html: The Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake (NHC) provides statutory first-loss residential building cover up to $300,000 + GST ($345,000 incl. GST) per dwelling at an annual levy capped at $480 + GST ($552.00 incl. GST), following $3.8B+ in insured losses from the 2023 North Island severe weather events.
natural-hazard-claims.official_data_summary: Natural Hazards Insurance Act 2023 Statutory Schedule: Building cap = $300,000 (excl. GST), max annual levy = $480 (excl. GST); 2023 North Island weather catastrophe insured losses = $3.8B+.
natural-hazard-claims.source_html:
HLF calculation: Cap incl. GST: $300,000 × 1.15 = $345,000 | Max Levy incl. GST: ($300,000 ÷ 100 × $0.16) × 1.15 = $552.00
Source: Natural Hazards Insurance Act 2023 (NZ Legislation) & Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake (NHC) • Glossary: Sum Insured & Income Protection • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

acc-weekly-compensation-claims.official_data_summary: ACC Annual Report (2025/26): Total accepted injury claims = 2,100,000+ (+1.6% YoY, including minor treatment-only claims); New weekly compensation entitlement claims = 105,000 (-1.9% from 107,000 in 2024/25).
acc-weekly-compensation-claims.source_html:
HLF calculation: 105,000 new weekly compensation claims ÷ 2,100,000 total accepted injury claims = 5.0 per 100 accepted claims (separate annual claim counts)
Source: Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) — Annual Report & Official Claim Statistics • Glossary: Sum Insured & Income Protection • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

acc-earners-levy-cap.html: For the 2026/27 tax year, the ACC Earners' Levy is $1.75 per $100 (1.75% incl. GST) up to a Maximum Liable Earnings cap of $156,641 (a maximum annual levy of $2,741.22), capping ACC's 80% weekly compensation at $125,312.80/year ($2,409.86/week gross).
acc-earners-levy-cap.official_data_summary: ACC / IRD 2026/27 Statutory Schedule: Earners' levy = $1.75 per $100 incl. GST ($1.52 excl. GST); Maximum liable earnings = $156,641 (vs $152,790 in 2025/26).
acc-earners-levy-cap.source_html:
HLF calculation: Max Levy: ($156,641 ÷ 100) × $1.75 = $2,741.22/yr | Max 80% Comp: $156,641 × 80% = $125,312.80/yr ($2,409.86/wk)
Source: Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) & Inland Revenue — Earners' Levy Statutory Schedule • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) · Sum Insured & Income Protection • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

acc-earners-levy-cap.methodology: Live-parsed from the official ACC and Inland Revenue PAYE / Earners' Levy schedule, multiplying the Maximum Liable Earnings cap by the GST-inclusive levy rate and by the 80% statutory weekly compensation rate.

kiwisaver-hardship-withdrawals.source_html:
HLF calculation: $47.9m × $1m ÷ 5,440 members = $8,805/member (FY2026 annual avg: $538.2m ÷ 52,330 = $10,285/member)

kiwisaver-contributions-10yr.html: Over the year ended 30 June 2026, total KiwiSaver contributions transferred to scheme providers reached $11.40B—up +123.5% from $5.10B in FY2016 (+67.2% after CPI inflation)—comprising $6.64B (58.2%) from employees, $3.72B (32.6%) from employers, and $1.04B (9.1%) in Crown contributions (with the statutory default rate at 3.5% EE / 3.5% ER from 1 April 2026 and the maximum annual Government contribution at $260.72).

fhb-income-by-dti-band.source_html:
HLF calculation: $383.0m total band income × $1m ÷ 2,655.4 total implied applications = $144,232 (reproducible from the 5 band rows; subject to RBNZ rounding)

new-build-consent-cost-by-type.html: Across New Zealand residential building consents (October 2026), average consented construction values (excluding land) were ~$594,000 for a stand-alone house (~188 m², or ~$3,160/m²), ~$396,000 for a townhouse, flat, or unit (~112 m², or ~$3,536/m²), ~$468,000 for an apartment (~88 m², or ~$5,318/m²), and ~$432,000 for a retirement village unit (~102 m², or ~$4,235/m²)—an overall average of ~$486,000 per dwelling (~$3,329/m²).

fhb-typical-income.html: In September 2026, the typical (borrower-weighted average) gross household income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications was $144,232.
fhb-typical-income.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Figures (pools rounded to $0.1m, averages to $1,000): TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 avg ($59.0m pool / 299.5 implied apps) | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 avg ($101.0m pool / 668.9 implied apps) | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 avg ($124.0m pool / 892.1 implied apps) | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 avg ($76.0m pool / 608.0 implied apps) | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000 avg ($23.0m pool / 187.0 implied apps).
fhb-typical-income.source_html:
HLF calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41) • Direct RBNZ C41 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

fhb-typical-income.definition: The typical (borrower-weighted mean) annual gross household income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications.
fhb-typical-income.calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding)
fhb-typical-income.formula: Total FHB Gross Income Pool ($m) × $1m ÷ Total Implied FHB Applications
fhb-typical-income.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because most first-home buyers apply as a couple (or with co-borrowers), RBNZ Borrower Gross Income reflects combined household income on the mortgage application—for example, two earners on ~$72,000 each equal ~$144,000 in gross application income.
fhb-typical-income.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C41 by summing total gross borrower income ($m) across all five first-home buyer Debt-to-Income bands and dividing by the total implied number of applications across those bands.
fhb-typical-income.summary_text: In September 2026, the typical (borrower-weighted average) gross household income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications was $144,232.

fhb-typical-dti.html: In September 2026, the typical New Zealand first-home buyer borrowed at an implied Debt-to-Income ratio of 4.0x–4.4x gross income ($573,678 average loan on $144,232 average gross income), with 90.9% of all first-home buyer lending written at or below 6x DTI.
fhb-typical-dti.official_data_summary: RBNZ Tables C31, C40 & C41 (September 2026): Average FHB loan = $573,678; Average FHB gross income = $144,232; FHB lending <= 6x TDTI = 90.9% (> 6x TDTI = 9.1%).
fhb-typical-dti.source_html:
HLF calculation: Implied FHB Mortgage DTI: $573,678 (C31 avg FHB loan) ÷ $144,232 (C41 avg FHB gross income) = 3.98x (~4.0x–4.4x total DTI) | C40 Share <= 6x DTI: 100.0% − 9.1% = 90.9%
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — DTI Purpose Use (Table C40) & Borrower Gross Income (Table C41) • Direct RBNZ C40 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) · Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

fhb-typical-dti.data_type: HLF-derived DTI ratio & band shares from official RBNZ Tables C31, C40 & C41
fhb-typical-dti.definition: The typical Debt-to-Income (DTI) multiple for approved New Zealand first-home buyers—measured both by the ratio of average FHB loan size to average FHB gross income and by the proportion of FHB lending written at or below 5x and 6x gross income in RBNZ Table C40.
fhb-typical-dti.calculation: Implied FHB Mortgage DTI: $573,678 (C31 avg FHB loan) ÷ $144,232 (C41 avg FHB gross income) = 3.98x (~4.0x–4.4x total DTI) | C40 Share <= 6x DTI: 100.0% − 9.1% = 90.9%
fhb-typical-dti.formula: Implied Mortgage DTI = Avg FHB Loan ÷ Avg FHB Gross Income; Share <= 6x DTI = 100% minus (>6x TDTI Share in C40)
fhb-typical-dti.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Most New Zealand first-home buyers borrow around 3.9x to 4.3x their gross household income—well below the 6.0x RBNZ owner-occupier speed-limit threshold—because bank servicing test rates cap borrowing power before the 6x DTI limit is reached.
fhb-typical-dti.methodology: Combines the implied FHB mortgage-to-income ratio (Average FHB Loan Size from Table C31 ÷ Average FHB Gross Borrower Income from Table C41) with the distribution of FHB commitments across TDTI bands <= 5x and <= 6x in RBNZ Table C40.
fhb-typical-dti.summary_text: In September 2026, the typical New Zealand first-home buyer borrowed at an implied Debt-to-Income ratio of 4.0x–4.4x gross income ($573,678 average loan on $144,232 average gross income), with 90.9% of all first-home buyer lending written at or below 6x DTI.

mortgage-excess-repayments.html: In the September 2026 quarter, New Zealand mortgage borrowers made $4.30B ($4,297m) in voluntary excess mortgage repayments above their contracted minimum schedules (down 3.0% year-on-year from $4.43B a year earlier)—equivalent to 58.4% on top of the $7.36B ($7,361m) paid in scheduled minimum principal-and-interest repayments (and bringing rolling 12-month voluntary excess repayments to $18.03B).
mortgage-excess-repayments.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C35 (September 2026 quarter): Quarterly voluntary excess mortgage repayments (excluding full loan discharges) = $4,297m ($4.30B; rolling 4 quarters = $18.03B).
mortgage-excess-repayments.source_html:
HLF calculation: Quarterly Excess Repayments (September 2026 quarter) = $4.30B ($4,297m; 12M rolling = $18.03B) | Ratio to Scheduled P&I: $4,297m ÷ $7,361m = 58.4% (36.9% of combined scheduled + excess repayments)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage loan reconciliation (Table C35) • Direct RBNZ C35 .xlsx • Glossary: HLF Financial & Mortgage Glossary • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

rent-vs-mortgage-interest-outgoings.html: In Stats NZ's Year ended June 2025 housing-cost release, renting households paid an average of $505.50/week in rent, while mortgaged homeowners paid $704.70/week—split between $452.10/week in mortgage interest and $252.60/week in principal equity paydown (meaning the average renter pays $53.40/week more in unrecoverable rent than the average homeowner pays in interest).

HLF calculation: Average Weekly Rent ($505.50/wk) minus Average Weekly Mortgage Interest ($452.10/wk) = +$53.40/wk (+$2,777/yr more dead rent than dead interest; plus $252.60/wk principal paydown)

bank-of-mum-and-dad-inheritance-benchmar.definition: The percentage of New Zealand households that have received an inheritance or a substantial monetary gift ($5,000 or more in the last 10 years), alongside the median net worth of recipient households versus self-funded households.
bank-of-mum-and-dad-inheritance-benchmar.calculation: Self-Funded Households = 55% (est. median ~$368,000) vs Transfer Recipients = 45% (Inheritance median $817,000; Gift+Inheritance median $984,000)
bank-of-mum-and-dad-inheritance-benchmar.formula: Self-Funded Household Share (%) = 100% minus Share Receiving Gift/Inheritance; Wealth Ratio = Recipient Median ÷ Overall Median
bank-of-mum-and-dad-inheritance-benchmar.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Roughly 55% of New Zealand households have never received a substantial gift or inheritance—meaning self-funded first-home buyers should benchmark their deposit progress against fellow self-made peers rather than gifted deposits.
bank-of-mum-and-dad-inheritance-benchmar.methodology: Sourced from Stats NZ's Household Net Worth transfers and gifts tables, isolating the 55% of households building wealth with zero family gift or inheritance from the 45% who received transfers.
bank-of-mum-and-dad-inheritance-benchmar.summary_text: According to Stats NZ's Household Net Worth transfers module, 55% of New Zealand households have built their position with zero inheritance or substantial family gift, while 45% have received an inheritance (32%, median net worth $817,000) or a substantial monetary gift of $5,000+ in the past 10 years (19%, median net worth up to $984,000).

student-loan-borrowing-power-drag.html: While the median New Zealand student loan balance is $18,301 (June 2026), banks must deduct the compulsory 12% student loan repayment on every dollar earned above $24,128/yr—meaning a borrower on $90,000 loses $7,905/year in net servicing cashflow (reducing maximum mortgage borrowing power by ~$89,830) even if only $5,000 remains on the loan.

mortgage-revolving-credit-balances.html: As at September 2026, New Zealand borrowers held $7.00B ($7,005m) in drawn residential revolving credit mortgage balances (representing 1.8% of all bank residential mortgage lending—comprising $5.74B [1.9%] across owner-occupiers and $1.27B [1.2%] across residential property investors) (down 3.9% year-on-year from $7.29B a year earlier).
mortgage-revolving-credit-balances.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table S32 (September 2026): Registered bank residential revolving credit drawn balances = $7,005m ($7.00B).
mortgage-revolving-credit-balances.source_html:
HLF calculation: Total Residential Revolving Credit (September 2026): $5,737m (Owner-Occupier) + $1,268m (Investor) = $7,005m ($7.00B) | Share of Housing Loans: $7,005m ÷ $399,563m = 1.8% (OO: 1.9%, Investor: 1.2%)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Banks: Assets – Loans by product (Table S32) • Direct RBNZ S32 .xlsx • Glossary: KiwiSaver First-Home Withdrawal • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

low-equity-margin-penalty-spread.html: In October 2026, the gap between New Zealand banks' advertised 1-year 'Standard' rate for low-deposit borrowers (5.54%, RBNZ Table B20) and 1-year 'Special' rate for borrowers with 20%+ equity (4.95%, Table B21) was +59 basis points (+0.59%)—costing a typical $573,678 first-home mortgage an extra ~$3,385/year until 20% equity is reached.

HLF calculation: 1Y Standard Rate (B20: 5.54%) − 1Y Special Rate (B21: 4.95%) = +0.59% (+59 bps, or ~$3,385/yr on a $573,678 FHB mortgage)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Standard (Table B20) vs Special (Table B21) Residential Mortgage Interest Rates • Direct RBNZ B20 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

low-equity-margin-penalty-spread.formula: Low-Equity Penalty Spread = Standard Rate (B20) minus Special Rate (B21); Annual Dollar Penalty =Spread × Typical FHB Loan
low-equity-margin-penalty-spread.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Once a homeowner who originally bought with a 10% deposit reaches 20% equity (through principal repayments or property value growth), requesting an equity revaluation removes the low-equity margin and unlocks Special rates.
low-equity-margin-penalty-spread.methodology: Derived live from RBNZ Table B20 and Table B21 by subtracting the 1-year and 2-year Special fixed rates from the corresponding Standard fixed rates.

fixed-vs-floating-rate-mix.formula: Fixed Share = Fixed Stock ÷ Total Stock; 12-Month Roll-Off = Fixed Loans Repricing <=12 Months ÷ Total Fixed Stock
fixed-vs-floating-rate-mix.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because nearly 90% of New Zealand mortgage debt is fixed—and roughly two-thirds of fixed loans roll off within 12 months—OCR changes transmit rapidly into household budgets as terms expire.
fixed-vs-floating-rate-mix.methodology: Compiled from RBNZ Table S33 residential mortgage stock repricing statistics, dividing fixed-rate mortgage balances by total residential mortgage balances and summing fixed-rate bands repricing within 12 months.
fixed-vs-floating-rate-mix.summary_text: As at September 2026, across New Zealand's $388.6B in bank loans secured by residential mortgage, 89.2% ($346.6B) was held on fixed interest rates and 10.8% ($42.0B) on floating rates—with 64.5% ($223.6B) of fixed-rate balances scheduled to reprice within 12 months.
fixed-vs-floating-rate-mix.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Fixed vs floating mortgage share & 12-month fixed rate roll-off (RBNZ Mortgage Stock)," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential Mortgage Lending by Interest Rate Type (Table S33) & Financial Stability Report. https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/fixed-vs-floating-rate-mix/ (checked 16 November 2026). cash-savings-vs-mortgage-offset-spread.html: In September 2026, New Zealand interest-bearing call savings accounts averaged 2.65% gross (1.78% after 33% RWT tax) compared with 4.82% in tax-free interest saved by offsetting a residential mortgage (RBNZ Table B30)—an after-tax advantage of +3.04% (~$912/year per $30,000 held in an offset or revolving credit account).
cash-savings-vs-mortgage-offset-spread.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table B30 & Retail Deposit Series (September 2026): Settled 1-year mortgage rate = 4.82%; Call savings rate = 2.65% gross (1.78% net after 33% RWT).
cash-savings-vs-mortgage-offset-spread.source_html:
HLF calculation: Settled 1Y Mortgage Rate (4.82%) minus After-Tax Call Savings Rate (2.65% × 0.67 = 1.78% at 33% RWT) = +3.04% net advantage (~$912/yr per $30,000 offset)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Call Savings Rates (B25), Term Deposit Rates (B26) & Settled Mortgage Rates (B30) • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) · Refinancing • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

cash-savings-vs-mortgage-offset-spread.calculation: Settled 1Y Mortgage Rate (4.82%) minus After-Tax Call Savings Rate (2.65% × 0.67 = 1.78% at 33% RWT) = +3.04% net advantage (~$912/yr per $30,000 offset)
cash-savings-vs-mortgage-offset-spread.formula: Net Offset Advantage (%) = Settled Mortgage Rate (B30) minus (Call Savings Rate [B25] × (1 − 0.33 RWT))
cash-savings-vs-mortgage-offset-spread.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because bank savings interest is taxed at your Resident Withholding Tax (RWT) or PIE rate while mortgage interest saved via an offset or revolving credit account is tax-free, holding $30,000 in an offset facility saves thousands more per year than a standard savings account.
cash-savings-vs-mortgage-offset-spread.methodology: Derived live from RBNZ Tables B25, B26, and B30, calculating the net after-tax yield on cash deposits versus the effective tax-free return of offsetting mortgage debt.
cash-savings-vs-mortgage-offset-spread.summary_text: In September 2026, New Zealand interest-bearing call savings accounts averaged 2.65% gross (1.78% after 33% RWT tax) compared with 4.82% in tax-free interest saved by offsetting a residential mortgage (RBNZ Table B30)—an after-tax advantage of +3.04% (~$912/year per $30,000 held in an offset or revolving credit account).

credit-card-limits-servicing-impact.calculation: Total Credit Limits = $21,150m ($21.15B) | Utilisation: $5,378m ÷ $21,150m = 25.4% | Unused Limits = $15,772m ($15.77B)
credit-card-limits-servicing-impact.formula: Utilisation Rate (%) = (Total Advances Outstanding ÷ Total Credit Limits) × 100; Unused Limits = Total Limits − Advances
credit-card-limits-servicing-impact.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: New Zealanders hold ~$21B in credit card limits but only use ~30% of them. Because NZ banks assess mortgage affordability assuming you spend 3% of your total credit limit every month ($300/mo on a $10,000 limit, even if the balance is $0), every $10,000 of unused card limit reduces mortgage borrowing power by ~$45,000.
credit-card-limits-servicing-impact.methodology: Extracted live from RBNZ Table C12 by comparing total credit limits ($m) against total credit card balances outstanding ($m). Unused credit limit equals Total Credit Limits minus Total Advances Outstanding.
credit-card-limits-servicing-impact.summary_text: In August 2026, total approved New Zealand credit card limits stood at $21.15B ($21,150m) with a 25.4% utilisation rate ($5.38B drawn)—leaving $15.77B ($15,772m) in unused credit card limits that banks still stress-test at 3% per month on mortgage applications.

fhb-income-akl-vs-nz.html: In September 2026, average gross borrower incomes across New Zealand first-home buyer Debt-to-Income bands ranged from $123,000 to $197,000, with an overall average of $144,232.
fhb-income-akl-vs-nz.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Figures (pools rounded to $0.1m, averages to $1,000): TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 avg ($59.0m pool / 299.5 implied apps) | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 avg ($101.0m pool / 668.9 implied apps) | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 avg ($124.0m pool / 892.1 implied apps) | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 avg ($76.0m pool / 608.0 implied apps) | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000 avg ($23.0m pool / 187.0 implied apps).
fhb-income-akl-vs-nz.source_html:
HLF calculation: $383.0m total band income × $1m ÷ 2,655.4 total implied applications = $144,232 (reproducible from the 5 band rows; subject to RBNZ rounding)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41) • Direct RBNZ C41 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

fhb-dti-above-6x.html: In September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($139.0m of $1,527.0m)—sitting 10.9 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.
fhb-dti-above-6x.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C40 (September 2026): FHB lending with TDTI > 6 = $139.0m out of $1,527.0m total FHB commitments.
fhb-dti-above-6x.source_html:
HLF calculation: $139.0m ÷ $1,527.0m = 9.1% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.1% = 10.9 pts)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income (DTI) purpose use (Table C40) • Direct RBNZ C40 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

fhb-dti-above-6x.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived >6x DTI share
fhb-dti-above-6x.definition: The percentage of total monthly first-home buyer mortgage lending value committed at a Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) ratio above 6x gross income, compared against the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap on non-exempt owner-occupier lending.
fhb-dti-above-6x.formula: (FHB Lending with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB Commitments across all TDTI bands) × 100; Headroom = 20.0% minus (>6x Share)
fhb-dti-above-6x.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because bank test servicing rates already constrain borrowing capacity, total FHB lending above 6x DTI sits well inside the 20% RBNZ speed-limit allowance.
fhb-dti-above-6x.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C40 by summing first-home buyer lending commitments in bands above 6x TDTI (including unknown TDTI) and dividing by total first-home buyer commitments across all TDTI bands.
fhb-dti-above-6x.summary_text: In September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($139.0m of $1,527.0m)—sitting 10.9 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.

build-cost-by-type.html: Across New Zealand residential building consents (October 2026), average consented construction values (excluding land) were ~$594,000 for a stand-alone house (~188 m², or ~$3,160/m²), ~$396,000 for a townhouse, flat, or unit (~112 m², or ~$3,536/m²), ~$468,000 for an apartment (~88 m², or ~$5,318/m²), and ~$432,000 for a retirement village unit (~102 m², or ~$4,235/m²)—an overall average of ~$486,000 per dwelling (~$3,329/m²).
build-cost-by-type.official_data_summary: Stats NZ Building Consents Value & Floor Area Series (October 2026, excluding land, GST-exclusive consent basis): Stand-alone house mean = ~$594,000 (~188 m²); Townhouse/flat/unit mean = ~$396,000 (~112 m²); Apartment mean = ~$468,000 (~88 m²); Retirement village unit mean = ~$432,000 (~102 m²).
build-cost-by-type.source_html:
HLF calculation: Stand-alone houses: $594,000 ÷ 188 m² = $3,160/m² | Townhouses/flats/units: $396,000 ÷ 112 m² = $3,536/m² | Apartments: $468,000 ÷ 88 m² = $5,318/m² | Retirement units: $432,000 ÷ 102 m² = $4,235/m² (consent build value excl. land)
Source: Stats NZ — Building Consents Issued (New Residential Dwelling Consent Values & Floor Area by Building Type) • Glossary: Turnkey vs Construction Loan • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

personal-insurance-average-claim.formula: Daily Claims Paid = Annual Claims Paid ÷ 365; Mean Annual Premium per Cover = Total Annual Life Premiums ÷ Total In-Force Covers
personal-insurance-average-claim.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Shows the scale of New Zealand's personal risk protection pool across Term Life, lump-sum Trauma cover, and monthly Income/Mortgage Repayment Protection supporting households through death, serious illness, and disability.
personal-insurance-average-claim.methodology: Automatically fetched and parsed from the latest Financial Services Council (FSC) Life Insurance Industry Spotlight PDF and cross-checked against RBNZ Table J10 life insurance series.
personal-insurance-average-claim.summary_text: According to the Financial Services Council (FSC) Life Insurance Industry Spotlight (September 2025), New Zealand life and personal risk insurers paid out $6.41B in annual claims ($17.56m per day).
personal-insurance-average-claim.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Life, Trauma & Income Protection annual claims paid, premiums & covers in force (FSC / RBNZ)," September 2025. fhb-low-deposit-share.html: In September 2026, 50.3% of first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) were written with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR), up from 46.0% a year earlier.
fhb-low-deposit-share.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 1,342 high-LVR (>80% LVR) FHB borrowers ($850m) out of 2,667 total FHB borrowers ($1,530m).
fhb-low-deposit-share.source_html:
HLF calculation: 1,342 ÷ 2,667 = 50.3% (Lending: $850m ÷ $1,530m = 55.6%)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
fhb-low-deposit-share.name: First-home buyers using under 20% deposit (>80% LVR)
fhb-low-deposit-share.also_known_as: Low-deposit first-home buyer mortgage share / High-LVR (>80%) FHB share
fhb-low-deposit-share.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31)
fhb-low-deposit-share.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived percentage share
fhb-low-deposit-share.definition: The percentage of new first-home buyer residential mortgage commitments approved by New Zealand registered banks with a loan-to-value ratio (LVR) above 80% (meaning a deposit of less than 20%).
fhb-low-deposit-share.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: First-home buyers are the primary recipients of bank low-deposit (>80% LVR) lending allowances, supplemented by LVR-exempt Kāinga Ora First Home Loans and new-build lending.
fhb-low-deposit-share.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 by dividing the monthly number of new first-home buyer mortgage commitments with LVR > 80% (LVRN.MMB2.BC1) by total monthly first-home buyer mortgage commitments (LVRN.MMB2.AC1), multiplied by 100.
fhb-low-deposit-share.summary_text: In September 2026, 50.3% of first-home mortgages approved across New Zealand (1,342 of 2,667 loans, or $850m in lending) were written with under a 20% deposit (>80% LVR), up from 46.0% a year earlier.
fhb-low-deposit-share.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "First-home buyers using under 20% deposit (>80% LVR)," September 2026. fhb-lending-share.html: In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 2,667 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $1.53B—accounting for 20.3% of all new residential mortgage lending (up from 19.2% a year earlier), with an average loan size of $573,678.
fhb-lending-share.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 2,667 FHB borrowers and $1,530m FHB lending out of $7,533m total new residential lending (LVRN.MMB1.AA).
fhb-lending-share.source_html:
HLF calculation: $1,530m ÷ $7,533m = 20.3% (Mean loan: $1,530m × $1m ÷ 2,667 = $573,678; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
fhb-lending-share.calculation_live: $1,530m ÷ $7,533m = 20.3% (Mean loan: $1,530m × $1m ÷ 2,667 = $573,678; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)

fhb-lending-share.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived share/mean
fhb-lending-share.definition: The share of total new residential mortgage lending value committed to first-home buyers across New Zealand, alongside the monthly number of first-home buyer loans and mean loan size.
fhb-lending-share.calculation: $1,530m ÷ $7,533m = 20.3% (Mean loan: $1,530m × $1m ÷ 2,667 = $573,678; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
fhb-lending-share.formula: (FHB Lending Value [LVRN.MMB1.AC1] ÷ All-Borrower Total Lending [LVRN.MMB1.AA]) × 100; Mean Loan = LVRN.MMB1.AC1 ÷ LVRN.MMB2.AC1
fhb-lending-share.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Tracks first-home buyer market participation relative to existing owner-occupiers and residential property investors.
fhb-lending-share.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 by dividing first-home buyer new lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AC1) by total new lending across all borrower types (LVRN.MMB1.AA). Mean loan size is LVRN.MMB1.AC1 (published by RBNZ rounded to $1m) divided by LVRN.MMB2.AC1.
fhb-lending-share.summary_text: In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 2,667 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $1.53B—accounting for 20.3% of all new residential mortgage lending (up from 19.2% a year earlier), with an average loan size of $573,678.

investor-lending-share.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C31 (September 2026): 2,668 investor borrowers and $1,335m investor lending out of $7,533m total lending (LVRN.MMB1.AA).
investor-lending-share.source_html:
HLF calculation: $1,335m ÷ $7,533m = 17.7%
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

investor-lending-share.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C31 by dividing monthly residential investor lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AN) by total new mortgage lending across all borrower types (LVRN.MMB1.AA).

refinance-share.html: In September 2026, 2,772 New Zealand mortgage holders switched lenders, refinancing $1.73B ($1,729m) in home loans—representing 23.0% of all new residential mortgage lending, at an average loan size of $623,737.
refinance-share.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Change in loan provider = 2,772 borrowers and $1,729m out of $7,533m total purpose lending (dollar series rounded to $1m).
refinance-share.source_html:
HLF calculation: $1,729m ÷ $7,533m = 23.0% (Mean loan: $1,729m × $1m ÷ 2,772 = $623,737; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33) • Direct RBNZ C33 .xlsx • Glossary: Refinancing · Usable Equity • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
refinance-share.calculation_live: $1,729m ÷ $7,533m = 23.0% (Mean loan: $1,729m × $1m ÷ 2,772 = $623,737; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
refinance-share.name: Mortgage refinancing (switching loan provider) share & volume
refinance-share.also_known_as: Bank-to-bank mortgage switching share, loan count & average refinance size
refinance-share.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33)
refinance-share.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived share/mean
refinance-share.definition: The share of new residential mortgage lending value and number of borrowers switching from one mortgage lender to another ('change in loan provider'), alongside the mean refinanced loan size.
refinance-share.calculation: $1,729m ÷ $7,533m = 23.0% (Mean loan: $1,729m × $1m ÷ 2,772 = $623,737; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
refinance-share.formula: (Change in Loan Provider Value [LVRN.MMB1.AZD] ÷ Total Lending by Purpose) × 100; Mean Loan = LVRN.MMB1.AZD ÷ LVRN.MMB2.AZD
refinance-share.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Refinancing volume measures how actively existing mortgage holders are comparing fixed rates and cashback offers across competing banks once their fixed terms expire.
refinance-share.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C33 by dividing 'change in loan provider' lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AZD) by the sum of all purpose categories (property purchase AZC, top-up AZB, change in provider AZD, and other AZE).
refinance-share.summary_text: In September 2026, 2,772 New Zealand mortgage holders switched lenders, refinancing $1.73B ($1,729m) in home loans—representing 23.0% of all new residential mortgage lending, at an average loan size of $623,737.
refinance-share.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Mortgage refinancing (switching loan provider) share & volume," September 2026. top-up-share.html: In September 2026, 9,639 homeowners were approved for a mortgage top-up on their existing property—accounting for 46.4% of all mortgage approvals across New Zealand, with an average top-up of $99,803.
top-up-share.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Top-up approvals = 9,639 borrowers ($962m) out of 20,763 total approvals.
top-up-share.source_html:
HLF calculation: 9,639 ÷ 20,763 = 46.4% (Mean top-up: $962m × $1m ÷ 9,639 = $99,803)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33) • Direct RBNZ C33 .xlsx • Glossary: Refinancing · Usable Equity • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
top-up-share.name: Mortgage top-up share of approvals & average top-up amount
top-up-share.also_known_as: Existing homeowner equity top-up approval share & mean top-up value
top-up-share.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33)
top-up-share.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived share/mean
top-up-share.definition: The percentage of all monthly residential mortgage approvals that are top-ups on an existing mortgage with the same lender, alongside the mean dollar top-up size.
top-up-share.formula: (Top-up Count [LVRN.MMB2.AZB] ÷ Total Approvals by Purpose) × 100; Mean Top-Up = LVRN.MMB1.AZB ÷ LVRN.MMB2.AZB
top-up-share.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Top-ups are one of the most common transactions in New Zealand banking—used by homeowners to fund renovations, deposits on investment properties, or major capital purchases.
top-up-share.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C33 by dividing top-up borrower count (LVRN.MMB2.AZB) by total mortgage approvals across all purposes, and dividing top-up lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AZB, rounded to $1m) by top-up borrower count.
top-up-share.summary_text: In September 2026, 9,639 homeowners were approved for a mortgage top-up on their existing property—accounting for 46.4% of all mortgage approvals across New Zealand, with an average top-up of $99,803.
top-up-share.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Mortgage top-up share of approvals & average top-up amount," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/top-ups/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.

interest-only-share.html: In September 2026, 31.5% of new residential investor mortgage lending was written on interest-only terms, compared with 13.7% for owner-occupiers.
interest-only-share.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C32 (September 2026): New investor interest-only = $420m of $1,335m; New owner-occupier interest-only = $828m of $6,064m.
interest-only-share.source_html:
HLF calculation: Investors: $420m ÷ $1,335m = 31.5% | Owner-Occupiers: $828m ÷ $6,064m = 13.7%
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New and existing residential mortgage lending by payment type (Table C32) • Direct RBNZ C32 .xlsx • Glossary: Interest-Only Mortgage · KiwiSaver First-Home Withdrawal • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
interest-only-share.name: Interest-only share of new investor vs owner-occupier mortgage lending
interest-only-share.also_known_as: Investor vs owner-occupier interest-only mortgage proportion (RBNZ C32)
interest-only-share.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New and existing residential mortgage lending by payment type (Table C32)
interest-only-share.source_series_ids: New Investor Interest-Only ÷ LVRN.MMB1.AN | New Owner-Occupier Interest-Only ÷ LVRN.MMB1.AC
interest-only-share.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived percentage shares
interest-only-share.definition: The percentage of new residential mortgage lending written on interest-only terms (including revolving credit facilities) for property investors compared with owner-occupiers.
interest-only-share.formula: (New Investor Interest-Only Lending ÷ Total New Investor Lending) × 100
interest-only-share.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Property investors frequently use interest-only terms on rental debt so cashflow can be directed toward repaying non-tax-deductible personal home loan debt first.
interest-only-share.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C32 by dividing new interest-only investor lending value by total new investor lending value, and new interest-only owner-occupier lending value by total new owner-occupier lending value.
interest-only-share.summary_text: In September 2026, 31.5% of new residential investor mortgage lending was written on interest-only terms, compared with 13.7% for owner-occupiers.

fhb-dti-headroom.html: In September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($139.0m of $1,527.0m)—sitting 10.9 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.
fhb-dti-headroom.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C40 (September 2026): FHB lending with TDTI > 6 = $139.0m out of $1,527.0m total FHB commitments.
fhb-dti-headroom.source_html:
HLF calculation: $139.0m ÷ $1,527.0m = 9.1% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.1% = 10.9 pts)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income (DTI) purpose use (Table C40) • Direct RBNZ C40 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
fhb-dti-headroom.name: First-home buyer high Debt-to-Income (>6x DTI) share vs 20% RBNZ speed limit
fhb-dti-headroom.also_known_as: FHB TDTI > 6 share of commitments & buffer below RBNZ DTI speed limit
fhb-dti-headroom.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income (DTI) purpose use (Table C40)
fhb-dti-headroom.source_series_ids: FHB New Commitments with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB New Commitments
fhb-dti-headroom.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived >6x DTI share
fhb-dti-headroom.definition: The percentage of total monthly first-home buyer mortgage lending value committed at a Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) ratio above 6x gross income, compared against the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap on non-exempt owner-occupier lending.
fhb-dti-headroom.formula: (FHB Lending with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB Commitments across all TDTI bands) × 100; Headroom = 20.0% minus (>6x Share)
fhb-dti-headroom.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because bank test servicing rates already constrain borrowing capacity, total FHB lending above 6x DTI sits well inside the 20% RBNZ speed-limit allowance.
fhb-dti-headroom.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C40 by summing first-home buyer lending commitments in bands above 6x TDTI (including unknown TDTI) and dividing by total first-home buyer commitments across all TDTI bands.
fhb-dti-headroom.summary_text: In September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($139.0m of $1,527.0m)—sitting 10.9 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.

fhb-borrower-income.source_html:
HLF calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding)

fhb-borrower-income.data_type: HLF-derived band-weighted mean from official RBNZ Table C41 bands
fhb-borrower-income.definition: The band-weighted mean annual gross borrower income across approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications and property investor applications, derived by HLF from RBNZ Table C41's Debt-to-Income bands.
fhb-borrower-income.calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding)
fhb-borrower-income.formula: Sum(Band Total Gross Income [$m]) ÷ Sum(Band Total Gross Income [$m] ÷ Band Average Gross Income [$k]) × 1,000
fhb-borrower-income.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: RBNZ's Borrower Gross Income (BGI) measures total application income (which for couples combines two salaries, and for investors includes existing salaries plus gross rental and other qualifying income).
fhb-borrower-income.methodology: RBNZ Table C41 publishes official total gross income ($m, rounded to $0.1m) and average gross income ($000, rounded to $1,000) within each TDTI band rather than a single all-bands average. HLF derives the overall mean by dividing total gross income summed across all reported TDTI bands by the implied number of applications (Band Total Income ÷ Band Average Income) summed across those bands.
fhb-borrower-income.summary_text: In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands).
fhb-borrower-income.citation: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs property investors," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage borrower gross income (BGI) (Table C41). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.

median-rent-nz.html: In September 2026, New Zealand's national median weekly private rent was $599/wk (up 1.5% year-on-year), with regional medians of $640/wk in Auckland, $580/wk in Wellington, and $560/wk in Canterbury.
median-rent-nz.official_data_summary: MBIE Tenancy Services (September 2026): National ('ALL') median weekly rent = $599/wk; Auckland = $640/wk; Wellington = $580/wk; Canterbury = $560/wk.
median-rent-nz.source_html:
HLF calculation: Reported national median = $599/wk; YoY = ($599 - $590) ÷ $590 = +1.5%
Source: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) — Tenancy Services Rental Bond Data • Glossary: Gross Rental Yield • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

median-rent-nz.methodology: Extracted from MBIE Tenancy Services' monthly regional rental bond dataset (Location = 'ALL' for national median), with year-on-year dollar and percentage changes calculated against the same month a year earlier.

kiwisaver-first-home-withdrawals.html: In September 2026, 4,250 KiwiSaver members withdrew a combined $195.7m toward a first home—an average of $46,047 per member (with annual first-home withdrawals growing over 10 years from $495.0m across 26,570 members in FY2016 to $2.27B across 50,470 members in FY2026).
kiwisaver-first-home-withdrawals.official_data_summary: Inland Revenue KiwiSaver Withdrawals (September 2026): First-home withdrawals = 4,250 members and $195.7m (FY2026: 50,470 members / $2.27B vs FY2016: 26,570 / $495.0m).
kiwisaver-first-home-withdrawals.source_html:
HLF calculation: Monthly mean: $195.7m × $1m ÷ 4,250 = $46,047/member | 10Y annual: $2,270m ÷ $495m = +358.6% nominal (+243.0% real ÷ 1.337 CPI)
Source: Inland Revenue — KiwiSaver Withdrawal Statistics (First Home Purchase) • Glossary: KiwiSaver First-Home Withdrawal • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.

kiwisaver-provider-switches.official_data_summary: Inland Revenue KiwiSaver Scheme Transfers (Year ended 30 June 2026): 198,897 inter-scheme transfers (vs 174,921 in FY2025 and 140,557 in FY2016).
kiwisaver-provider-switches.source_html:
HLF calculation: Monthly mean: 198,897 ÷ 12 = 16,575/mth | 10Y growth: (198,897 − 140,557) ÷ 140,557 = +41.5%

kiwisaver-average-balance.html: As at 31 March 2026, total KiwiSaver funds under management reached $138.8B across 3.44 million members, with an average member balance of $40,340—up +213.9% (+12.1%/yr) from $12,852 in 2016 (+134.8%, or +8.9%/yr, after CPI inflation).
kiwisaver-average-balance.official_data_summary: FMA KiwiSaver Annual Report 2026 (year ended 31 March 2026, published 10 September 2026): Official average member balance = $40,340; Total FUM = $138.8B across 3.44m members (vs $12,852 / $33.8B in March 2016).
kiwisaver-average-balance.source_html:
HLF calculation: Nominal 10Y: ($40,340 − $12,852) ÷ $12,852 = +213.9% (+12.1%/yr) | Real 10Y (÷1.337 CPI): ($40,340 ÷ $17,183) − 1 = +134.8% (+8.9%/yr)
Source: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) — KiwiSaver Annual Report & RBNZ Table T43 • Direct RBNZ T43 .xlsx • Glossary: KiwiSaver First-Home Withdrawal • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 16 November 2026.
